title: ezDIC: Lightweight Virtual Extensometer for Linear Strain Extraction from Image Sequences
access_conditions: Access is granted for authorized research or teaching use. Contact Dr. Delun Gong for permission before redistribution, reuse outside the authorized context, or derivative use.
description:
ezDIC is a lightweight dual-mode workstation for image sequences. The virtual-extensometer mode tracks two user-defined ROI markers and exports engineering strain, true strain, and quality-control results. The full-field mode correlates each deformation frame to one fixed reference frame, samples a rectangular ROI on a POI grid with IC-GN or IC-LM, and exports displacement and strain maps under dic/ for frames with a finite strain field.

Full-field coordinates and displacements are in px; strain components are dimensionless, and Exy/exy are tensor shear components. The fixed full-field core outputs are tabular data plus u/v/Exx/Eyy/Exy maps. An Exx overlay is optional. The result is a POI grid, not a per-pixel or 3D measurement.

Failed tracking frames and failed POIs remain NaN rather than being silently interpolated. A full-field frame with no finite strain points is skipped as a failed frame, and a run with no finite strain points fails instead of being reported as completed.
